label: thm:borromean-character-fibre
title: Two values of the standard character determine the Borromean conjugacy class
html:
Let \chi_{(2,1)}(q, w) be the trace of a word w in the (2,1) representation of the Hecke algebra H_3(q). Let w be a word in \sigma_0^{\pm 1}, \sigma_1^{\pm 1} of any length with writhe 0. If

  \chi_{(2,1)}(i, w) = \chi_{(2,1)}(i, \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  \chi_{(2,1)}(2, w) = \chi_{(2,1)}(2, \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}),

then w is conjugate in B_3 to \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3.

Proof

At q = i the character of a writhe-0 word equals the trace of its image under the Burau representation B_3 \to \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z}) at t = -1; for \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} that trace is 18. Every matrix of trace greater than 2 is conjugate to a product of R = \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix} and L = \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}. A product with r factors R and l factors L has trace at least 2 + rl, and exactly 2 + l (or 2 + r) when only one R (or one L) occurs.

The kernel of B_3 \to \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z}) is generated by \Delta^4, which has writhe 12. Lifting the conjugacy back to B_3 therefore costs a power of \Delta^4, and writhe 0 forces r \equiv l \pmod{12}. With rl \le 16 this leaves r = l \le 4. A check over the 340 words with r = l \le 4 leaves (RL)^3, the image of \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}, and R^4L^4. The character is a class function on B_3, and R^4L^4 has a different value at q = 2.
